title: Active Record

validation.research: Six authoritative source notes. Fowler’s Active Record entry in Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture establishes the record object combining row data, domain behavior, and database access. Rails official basics, validation, transaction, and optimistic-locking documentation supplies concrete framework behavior and qualifications: construction versus persistence, model uniqueness checks versus database constraints, connection-scoped transactions, object state after rollback, and configured version protection. Official Python SQLite documentation supports this implementation’s caller-owned transaction and connection lifetime. The article distinguishes the pattern from Rails’s particular API; its Python example and native diagrams are original teaching material.
validation.python_examples: Both actual article fences execute as task.py and demo.py and produce six stated lines exactly. Checks cover printable title boundaries, Boolean completion and positive generated IDs, read-only public properties, invalid rename preservation, local no-rename-after-completion policy, idempotent completion, unsaved construction without SQL, memory changes without automatic save, new insert versus existing update, unchanged-row update behavior, missing/corrupt rows and propagated storage errors, parameterized quoted titles, no hidden commit, assigned IDs retained after rolled-back inserts, object/row divergence after rollback, multiple-record caller rollback, committed cross-connection visibility, and failure when persisting through a closed connection. An explicit stale copy overwrites later completion state, demonstrating that the local rule is not a concurrency guarantee and that no version protection is supplied.

example_limits: Python 3.10+ and standard-library SQLite. Original Task policy uses 1–80 printable nonblank title characters, Boolean completion, and positive generated integer IDs. Public properties are read-only; business methods change local state and save issues insert/update SQL. The caller owns commit, rollback, and connection closing. Construction and completion do not save; save does not commit. Rollback does not rewind object fields or clear assigned IDs in this implementation, so affected objects need reloading or discarding. The rename guard checks loaded local state, not current database state. No deletion, callbacks, associations, identity caching, authorization, expected-version check, automatic retry, or cross-database atomicity is implemented. The hand-written API is not a Rails reproduction.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
